title: Ruby Cannot Swim, But She Jumped Into The Pool Anyway . . . (Episode 3)
caption:
In Love Next Door episode 3, Ruby tells her old principal she still works at Greip.
The truth comes out at an empty swimming pool, where Ethan has a teenage letter of his own. Follow for episode 4!

#lovenextdoor #kdrama #kdramarecap #spoilerroom #fyp
comment: Was Ethan right to call Ruby out for taking her old kind of job again? Why?

segments.say: Ruby can't swim. She jumps into the pool anyway, and Ethan has to *grab* her before she sinks.
To see how it got here, go back to Ethan dreaming about his old *swim meet*.
Ethan wakes at three in the *morning* to Ruby yelling next door. She even shouts a movie spoiler through the window.
Next morning at the office, Max cheers about a huge retirement home offer. Ethan only worries about his dying pomegranate *tree*.
Over at Ruby's house, Linda rolls kimbap and tells Frank her new plan. Stop pushing Ruby, and wait for her to *cave*.
Ruby just writes a schedule for her unemployed life. Games, TV, space out, and a *nap*.
She treats doing nothing like a full-time *job*.
Bored, she calls Ethan, and he hangs up on her. So she finds Mia at a comic shop *instead*.
Ruby wants something red. Mia thinks she means the adults-only shelf, but Ruby means *blood*.
Then Ethan walks in and says he only came for a book. The book is a comic called *Princess*.
Then Ethan and Mia both have somewhere to be. Ruby walks home alone. Having no job gets *lonely* fast.
The next morning, Ruby's old homeroom teacher, Ms. Yu, walks into the kimbap shop. She is the *principal* now.
Ms. Yu orders forty dishes, and Ruby offers to carry them to the *school*.
On the way, Ms. Yu says every teacher is proud that Ruby works at Greip. Ruby just *smiles*.
Ethan is there too, because his firm entered the school's gym design contest. Then Ms. Yu asks Ruby to talk to the *students*.
A student asks what she wanted to be in high school. Ruby has no *answer*. She never once asked herself.
After class, Ethan drags her to the schoolyard to dig up their old time *capsule*.
They dig for half an hour and find *nothing*. Ruby asks why he played along with her lie.
Ethan says her years at Greip were *real*. That is good enough advice for the kids.
Ruby gives up and walks off. Ethan keeps digging *alone*.
At home, Linda's wrist is wrapped in pain patches, and even Danny has a job now. Only Ruby is doing *nothing*.
That night, Ethan works on the school pool. Max tells him to focus on the retirement home. But that offer has a *catch*.
Across town, Mia's ambulance is stuck in traffic with a sick kid *inside*.
Then a stranger in a white shirt runs between the cars and clears a *path*.
At the station, Mia gushes about the stranger. Then rice cakes arrive from the man she treated in the *park*.
At the client meeting, Ethan finds out the catch. The client wants them to copy famous foreign designs and call it an *homage*.
Ethan calls it plagiarism. Later, in the garage, Max says to fake it, then swap in their own *design*. That was never going to work.
Ethan says he is protecting his staff's pride. Max says they need *salaries*. Neither of them is wrong.
Then it gets personal. Max says Ethan only cares about that old *pool*.
Ethan walks away without a *word*.
Meanwhile, a recruiter takes Ruby out for tea. She offers two jobs, and both look just like her old *one*.
Later, Ethan runs into her on the street. He asks if she really wants that kind of *work* again.
Ruby snaps. Dreams are a luxury, she says, and he has always had an easy *life*.

segments.text: I've had winters like that too.

segments.say: Here is why. Years ago, Ruby gave teenage Ethan a towel stitched with his name for the 2008 *Olympics*.
On his way to training, a car hits him. He survives, but his swimming career is *over*.
So he really did know *winter*.
Next morning, Nina from the office tells Ethan his big dreams come from *privilege*.
It sounds just like Ruby in the park. Ethan admits whoever said it was *right*.
Then Max comes to apologize, and so does Ethan. They laugh and agree to stay *together*.
Then both companies ask Ruby for an interview. She stares at the message and does not *smile*.
That night, Ruby is back at the school looking for the capsule, and she runs into Ms. Yu in the *dark*.
Over pear tea, Ruby admits the lie. She quit Greip, or maybe she was *chased out*.
Ms. Yu says kids always find their own answers, so Ruby should trust her *choice*.
Then she says Ethan might be at the old *pool*.
At the empty pool, Ethan has Ruby's teenage letter, and he is reading it out *loud*.
Ruby chases him to get it back. So he jumps into the pool, clothes and all, with the letter in his *hand*.
Ruby can't swim, so she can't follow. Ethan says it is his first time in a pool since he quit *swimming*.
Then he asks if she remembers the month he locked himself in his *room*.
Ruby would not give up. She climbed along the window ledge to reach *him*.
She calls him a loser until he finally yells *back*. It is the first time he has spoken in a month.

segments.text: Lock your door again, and I'll break it down.

segments.say: Back in the pool, Ruby does the same thing. She jumps in without *thinking*. Some habits never change.
Ethan grabs her before she sinks, and tells her to *relax*.
Soon she is floating on her back, and Ethan holds her *up*.
Floating there, Ruby admits she feels like nothing without her old *job*.
Ethan says he felt the same after he quit swimming. Alone at the starting line. But he found a new place to *swim*.
Then Ethan asks two what-ifs. Would she go back to Greip? No. Would she undo the engagement? Still *no*.
Then the story jumps back to the day they all wrote letters to their future *selves*.
Teenage Ethan's letter asks one thing. Has he told Ruby how he *feels*?
And the time capsule Ruby could not find? Ethan dug it up on his *own*.
